 THESE APPEALS COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The claimants are in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the District and Sessions Judge and Additional MACT, Bidar sitting at Basavakalyan (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC Nos.171/2015 and 172/2015 by common judgment and award dated 06.01.2015.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claimants were riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-12/B-4316 on 23.10.2014.
At about 7.30 a.m. on the said date, the driver of a multi-utility vehicle bearing registration No.MH-13/AZ-4986 (henceforth referred as 'offending vehicle') dashed against the motorcycle.
As a result, the claimants fell from the bike and suffered injuries and were treated as inpatients at different hospitals.
The claimants contended that they were employed as cooks in a Dhaba and were earning Rs.9,000/- per month.
They claimed that due to the injuries, they could not work as cooks in the Dhaba and hence, they were deprived of their income.

They also contended that the injuries had left them disabled and hence, NC: 2023:KHC-K:5595 filed claim petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
3. The owner did not contest the claim petitions.
4. The insurer contested the claim petitions and denied the accident as well as the averments made therein.
It contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid licence.
It also contended that the accident was due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by its rider and therefore, it was not liable to indemnify the owner of the offending vehicle.
5. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petitions were set down for trial.
The claimants were examined as PWs.1 and 2 respectively.

They examined the doctor who treated them as P.W.3 and he deposed that the claimant in MVC No.171/2015 had suffered disability to the extent of 23% and the claimant in MVC No.172/2015 had suffered disability to the extent of 19%.
The insurer did not lead any evidence.
6. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to rash and negligent NC: 2023:KHC-K:5595 driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

It also held that the claimant in MVC No.171/2015 had suffered fracture of right femur while the claimant in MVC Pundalik S/O Yadav @ Yadappa Kyase vs Ajeemkhan Patel S/O Rustum Khan And Anr on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149042320/
3 No.172/2015 had suffered fracture of right mandible malleolus.

the claimants are in appeal.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the claimants contended that the claimants were employed as cooks in a Dhaba and therefore, the injuries caused to them had left them disabled and they were deprived of the amenities of life.
She contended that the compensation therefore deserves to be enhanced.

She also contended that the Tribunal committed an error in considering the notional income of the claimants at a sum of Rs.3,000/-
per month while in similar circumstances, this Court has considered the notional income at a sum of Rs.7,500/- per month.
Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not warrant any enhancement.
10. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants as well as learned counsel for the insurer.
11. The insurer has not challenged the finding regarding negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle and its involvement in the accident.

The fact that the claimants suffered injuries in the accident is not denied by the insurer and the same is proved beyond doubt as per Exs.P.5, P.9,
P.15 and P.16.

The fact that claimant in MVC No.171/2015 had suffered facture of femur and the claimant in MVC No.172/2015 had suffered fracture of right mandible malleolus must have caused some amount of discomfort and disability to the claimants.
Though P.W.3 deposed that the claimants had suffered disability to the extent of 23% and 19% respectively, the Tribunal had rightly considered the disability at 10% to the whole body.

However, the Tribunal must have considered the notional income for the purpose of determining the compensation at a sum of Rs.7,500/- per month as is done by NC: 2023:KHC-K:5595 this Court in similar cases.
Likewise, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads was meager and deserves to be enhanced.
In view of the above, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is re-
determined as follows:

In MVC No.171/2015:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No. (In Rs.)
 1 Pain and suffering 40,000/-
 2 Attendant, nourished food and 10,000/-
 conveyance charges

3 Medical expenses 95,000/-
 4 Loss of income during laid up 22,500/-
 period (Rs.7,500x3)
 5 Loss of income due to disability 1,62,000/-
 (Rs.7,500x12x10%x18)

6 Loss of amenities 30,000/-
 Total 3,59,500/-

In view of the above, the appeals filed by the claimants are allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.2,10,800/- and Rs.1,51,800/- awarded by the Tribunal in MVC Nos.171/2015 and 172/2015 are enhanced to a sum of Rs.3,59,500/- and Rs.2,85,500/- respectively, which is payable by the insurer of the offending vehicle along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petitions till the date of realization.

The enhanced compensation along with accrued interest shall be deposited by the insurer of the offending vehicle before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the names of the claimants in any nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
